recognize_zh: 抹片左下有一條長弧形、淡藍灰色的細胞外結晶，右上有一個胞質深藍、邊緣不規則的漿細胞樣細胞，背景紅血球多處疊成錢串狀（rouleaux），符合漿細胞白血病的免疫球蛋白結晶。
features: Large extracellular elongated curved pale blue-gray crystal spanning several red cell diameters
Single cell with intensely basophilic cytoplasm and irregular cytoplasmic projections (upper right), consistent with a circulating plasma cell
Rouleaux formation with red cells stacked in short chains
Nuclear detail of the plasma cell is obscured by the deeply basophilic cytoplasm at this magnification
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large extracellular, elongated, curved pale blue-gray crystalline structure spanning several red cell diameters. A circulating cell with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and irregular cytoplasmic blebs is present, consistent with a plasma cell, although nuclear detail is limited in this image. Red cells show conspicuous rouleaux formation, reflecting increased serum paraprotein. Findings are consistent with extracellular immunoglobulin crystals in the setting of plasma cell leukemia.

ddx.vs: Cryoglobulins usually appear as amorphous pale blue-gray extracellular clumps rather than sharply defined elongated crystals, though both reflect paraprotein and can coexist.
Artifactual fibers are refractile and irregular in thickness, whereas these crystals take up stain uniformly and occur repeatedly across fields.

ddx.dx: Crystal-storing histiocytosis or intracellular plasma cell crystals
ddx.vs: Those crystals are intracytoplasmic within histiocytes or plasma cells, while the crystal here is free in the background.
Reactive plasmacytoid lymphocytes occur in viral illness without rouleaux or paraprotein crystals and are not accompanied by circulating clonal plasma cells.
